newsitem.title: USA: Bay Apartment Q4 shr $0.31 vs $0.18.
newsitem.headline: Bay Apartment Q4 shr $0.31 vs $0.18.

text.p: Bay Apartment Communities said Friday that revised definition Funds From Operations (FFO) per share on a weighted average, fully diluted basis increased about 19 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 over comparable FFO per share in the fourth quarter of 1995.

For the quarter ended December 31, 1996, Bay reported revised definition FFO of $12,302,000, or $.56 per share on a weighted average, fully diluted basis versus FFO of $6,532,000, or $.47 per share on the same basis for the fourth quarter of fiscal 1995.
FFO for the third quarter of 1996 was $10,831,000, or $.55 per share. FFO per share for all of 1996 was $2.15, a 20 percent increase over FFO per share of $1.79 in 1995.

The company noted that these FFO per share increases occurred even though Bay has substantially increased the number of fully diluted shares outstanding during 1996 and significantly deleveraged its balance sheet.

The calculation of FFO per share for the fourth quarter of 1996 on a weighted average, fully diluted basis reflects the effect of the company's sales of 1,661,414 shares of common stock and 405,022 shares of Series B Preferred Stock in May 1996 and the company's public offering of 5,750,000 shares of common stock in August 1996.

These transactions, along with other events, increased the company's weighted average, fully diluted shares outstanding by about 58.0 percent over those at the end of the fourth quarter of fiscal 1995.

These transactions also reduced the company's total debt to total market capitalization from about 40.4 percent at the end of the fourth quarter of 1995 to 25.9 percent at the end of the fourth quarter of 1996.

Bay also announced that on January 22, 1997, the company agreed to sell 1.4 million shares of common stock in an underwritten public offering at $37.125 per share. The offering is scheduled to close on January 28 and generate gross proceeds of $51,975,000 and net proceeds to the company, after all anticipated issuance costs, of approximately $49,271,000 -- before the exercise of the underwriter's over-allotment option.

Proceeds will be used to reduce unsecured acquisition and construction line of credit with the Union Bank of Switzerland and other banks. After this offering, the company's total debt to total market capitalization will be approximately 22 percent.
For the fourth quarter of 1996, Bay reported net income of $7,014,000, or $.31 per share, compared with net income of $3,000,000, or $.18 per share, for the same period a year ago.
